summary: JClaw bounds every child run three ways (idle budget, operator-only wall-clock ceiling, breadth/depth caps refused BEFORE anything is created), reconciles anything left RUNNING after a restart to FAILED with a distinct reason, and sweeps orphaned OS processes by command-line signature with SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation and an explicit live-process exclusion that it had to add after the sweep killed its own test server (2026-09-14). All of it is built and pinned by tests. Our fan-out accounting is already stronger than JClaw's (JClaw's batch collect counts misses in `count`; its LOST detector returns 0 on a DB error), so the transferable value is not accounting but LIFECYCLE BOUNDS we lack: no orphan-process sweep anywhere in our three locations (the machine has already been thrashed by ~12 leaked dev servers and a 2-hour-old `python3 -m http.server 8899` was alive during this study), no agent cap in measure-refute (100 units x 5 lenses would queue 600 agents on an 8 GB / 8-core box whose runtime cap is 6 concurrent), build-loop cycles run with no --max-turns by default (a node with no stop condition, by our own rule), and build-loop's CYCLE_RUNNING marker has no staleness rule so a kill -9 leaves a marker that says 'wait' forever. Four small adoptions, two of them one-line; the rest of JClaw's lifecycle machinery is runtime-owned in Claude Code and not expressible from a script.

candidates.pattern: Orphan-process sweep by command-line signature: list candidates, EXCLUDE live ones explicitly, SIGTERM, wait, escalate to SIGKILL, and kill the whole tree (descendants snapshotted before the parent dies).
candidates.failurePrevented: Leaked processes from dead runs thrashing an 8 GB machine (already bitten: ~12 orphaned vite/http.server/node processes 4-5 days old on 2026-09-10), and the opposite failure JClaw hit on 2026-09-14 — a sweep that kills a LIVE run because the signature matched.

Sweep by process signature instead"; jclaw.sh:3124 `candidates=$(pgrep -f "application.path=${SCRIPT_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true)`; :3127-3129 `case "$(ps -o command= -p "$pid" ...)" in *-Dplay.id=test*) continue ;;`; :3135-3141 `kill "$pid"` ... `sleep 3` ... `echo "pid $pid ignored SIGTERM — escalating to kill -9."`. candidates.builtAndExercised: Built. candidates.ourEvidence: Searched SSHD 1-1 and agent-harness (`grep -rn -i -E "orphan|pkill|lsof|ps aux|ps -ef"` over *.md,*.js,*.mjs,*.ts,*.sh,*.json,pre-commit*): zero hits outside npc test names. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ship-bar.md, settings.json: no orphan/process rule, no SessionEnd/Stop hook (settings.json has only a UserPromptSubmit hook). The only record is memory project-orphaned-processes-and-tunnel.md: "~12 ORPHANED PROCESSES on a machine with 64 MB free RAM ... no auditor thought to run `ps` until asked". Live measurement during this study: `ps -eo pid,etime,command | grep -E 'vite|http\.server|run-pipeline'` -> pid 75716 `Python -m http.server 8899 --bind 127.0.0.1` etime 02:03:23, spawned by a `/bin/sh -c ... &` tool call — the leak pattern recurs today. We DO kill a process group in one place: agent-harness/harness/chaos/chaos.mjs:184 `process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGTERM') // the whole group: npx → runner → workers` (spawned `detached: true`, :215); SSHD scripts/gates/chaos.ts:114-118 uses `execFileSync('npx', ['vitest', ...], { timeout: 900_000 })` which signals only the direct child — RESUME_HERE already lists this as a hole not yet ported.
candidates.proposal: agent-harness `harness/sweep-orphans.sh` (~40 lines, POSIX sh + pgrep/ps only, zero deps), symlinked into SSHD `scripts/`. Default is DRY-RUN: print pid, etime, command for processes matching a signature list (`vite`, `http.server`, `node .*run-`, `cloudflared tunnel --url`) older than `--min-age` (default 6h), EXCLUDING any pid whose ancestor chain contains a live `claude` process (JClaw's `play.id=test` exclusion, generalised). `--kill` sends SIGTERM to the process GROUP (`kill -- -$pgid`), sleeps 3, escalates to `kill -9` and prints which pids ignored TERM. No hook, no per-turn tokens; run it from the session-kickoff playbook line and after any workflow death.
candidates.doneCriterion: 1) With the 8899 http.server running: `sh harness/sweep-orphans.sh` lists it and exits 0 without killing (ps count unchanged). 2) `sh harness/sweep-orphans.sh --kill` -> `ps -p 75716` returns 1. 3) A dummy `sleep 99999 &` started from the current claude session is LISTED as excluded and never killed. 4) A test (`sweep-orphans.test.mjs`) spawns two detached dummies (one under a fake 'claude' parent) and asserts only the unparented one dies — the same two-dummy proof JClaw's commit describes.
candidates.cost: ~1 h to write + test; 0 tokens/turn (not a hook); zero runtime dependencies; one new file in agent-harness plus a symlink in SSHD.
candidates.why: The failure has already bitten this machine and nothing in our three locations detects it — a clear GAP. JClaw's version is JVM-specific (`application.path=`), so adapt the SHAPE (signature list + age + live-exclusion + TERM->KILL + group kill), not the code. Dry-run default and live-exclusion are non-negotiable: JClaw's own sweep killed a live test server the first time it was wrong, and our chaos.mjs already proves the group-kill idiom works here.

candidates.pattern: Every spawned run carries an absolute ceiling set by the OPERATOR, not by the run itself, independent of activity — on top of any activity-based budget.
candidates.failurePrevented: A runaway child that keeps producing activity (or keeps taking turns) and never stops — the 'node with no stop condition' our global rule calls a bug. JClaw's idle budget alone could never trip on an active child, so the ceiling was added as a separate, LLM-unsettable bound.

candidates.ourEvidence: Workflow runtime (workflow-authoring reference, loaded this study): `budget` is a HARD ceiling ("once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw") but only when the user passes a '+500k'-style directive (`budget.total` is null otherwise); a 1000-agent lifetime cap and a concurrency cap of min(16, CPUs-2) — on this box `sysctl hw.ncpu` = 8 -> 6 concurrent. `agent()` opts are `label, phase, schema, model, effort, isolation, agentType` — no per-agent timeout or turn cap exists to set. Stamp the value into the cycle header line written to loop.log so a postmortem shows the bound the cycle ran under.
candidates.doneCriterion: `grep -n -- '--max-turns' scripts/build-loop.sh` shows an unconditional flag with a numeric default; `sh -n scripts/build-loop.sh` exits 0; a dry cycle header in docs/loop/loop.log carries `max-turns=80`. Ceiling proven by running one cycle with `LOOP_MAX_TURNS=2` and reading `[loop] claude exit=` after it stops early.
candidates.why: Our own global rule says 'A node with no stop condition is a bug' and build-loop.sh — the only spawner we control end-to-end, explicitly meant to run unattended overnight — ships with the ceiling off. JClaw's design point that matters is that the ceiling is the operator's default, not an opt-in the run can forget. Nothing to adopt for Workflow agents: the runtime owns their bounds and exposes no per-agent knob.

candidates.pattern: Breadth cap enforced at spawn time for the WHOLE fan-out: refuse before anything is created when running + requested exceeds the cap, with a message naming the numbers.
candidates.failurePrevented: One call saturating the executor — on our machine, a large units x lenses product queueing hundreds of agents on 6 concurrent slots of an 8 GB box, burning a full usage window with no way to bank early results.

antiPatterns.what: Fail-open counts in the batch collect: `subagent_yield` over many runs reports a miss as an inline entry and then sets `count` to the size of the results list INCLUDING the misses — a caller reading `count == N` reads a run where some children were never collected as fully collected.
antiPatterns.evidence: app/tools/SubagentAsyncRunner.java:232-238 `if (f == null) { var miss = ...; miss.put(FIELD_STATUS, "UNKNOWN"); miss.put(FIELD_ERROR, "no pending async subagent ..."); results.add(miss); continue; }` then :257-259 `payload.put("results", results); payload.put("count", results.size());` — no live/miss split, no null.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: This is exactly the failure our accounting was rebuilt to prevent: measure-refute.js returns `fatalCount: null` unless EVERY verdict is live and an `integrity` string with live/expected counts ("5/6 live verdicts ... 1 UNVERIFIED", pinned in measure-refute.test.mjs:62-71). Keep ours; do not import a `count` that counts misses.
